sections.html:
Logan County is central Illinois farm country. Lincoln is both the county seat and its largest city, and Atlanta and Mount Pulaski round out the list. I-55 links Lincoln to Bloomington and Springfield, and Amtrak stops at Lincoln Station. Land area is about 618 square miles.

Expect 126 freezing days a year, which is why inspectors on a Logan County house pay close attention to the roof, gutters and foundation.

sections.h2: Which county offices handle your tax bill
sections.html:
Three Lincoln offices split the job.

  • Supervisor of Assessments (122 N. McLean St., 217-732-9635): directs the township assessors, keeps tax maps and parcel record cards, grants exemptions and serves as clerk to the Board of Review.
  • County Clerk (courthouse Room 20, 217-732-4148): applies each levy to the assessed base to produce rates, and handles redemption of tax sale certificates.
  • County Treasurer (courthouse Room 11, 217-732-3761): mails bills, takes payments, logs granted appeals and distributes the money.

The Treasurer also serves as county collector for real estate, mobile home and drainage tax. Every owner pays county, township and road and bridge tax. Schools, fire protection and other districts add to that, so your rate depends on which boundaries enclose your parcel.

Billing runs a year behind: money collected in 2026 pays for tax year 2025. The same sequence returns every year.

  • Real estate bills are mailed in May.
  • Installment one is due June 15 and installment two September 1, and a missed one picks up a 1.5% penalty for each month.
  • Mobile home bills leave the office at the end of March, with payment due June 1. After that day a $25 penalty applies, and another $25 is added each month, capped at $100.
  • The annual tax sale takes place in the fall, and buyers must register about two weeks ahead.

Logan County has elected, under Public Act 104-0553, to take delinquent real estate taxes as trustee for the taxing districts. If you missed a due date, call the Treasurer for today's payoff, because the penalty grows monthly.

Whichever way you pay, have the stub from your bill. The options:

  • The counter in courthouse Room 11, with cash or check. Real estate tax only can go on a card, which costs 2.35% plus $1.50.
  • The drop box on N. Kickapoo St. facing Latham Park, or the boxes on the north and south sides of the courthouse. No cash in the boxes.
  • Local banks, with the exception of Regions and CEFCU.
  • Mail, where the postmark counts as the date received.
  • Card or e-check by phone at 217-203-8359 with your property index number, or through the link on the Treasurer's web page.

Not receiving a bill does not excuse it. Under 35 ILCS 200/21-15 a postmark on or before the due date makes a mailed payment timely, and installment one is delinquent only after the later of June 1 or the day following the printed date.

sections.h2: How a Logan County bill is built
sections.html:
Township and county assessors set the assessed value. The abstract then goes to the state, which may apply a multiplier that raises, lowers or leaves values unchanged. For each district the County Clerk divides the levy by assessed valuation to get a rate, subject to any statutory cap. Multiply the combined rate by your equalized assessed value and you have the tax.

Homes are assessed at one-third of market value, and equalization factors from the Supervisor keep levels there. Board of Review rules set a four-year reassessment cycle for each parcel, with yearly reassessment permitted. Each year's assessment changes are published in the Lincoln Courier.

Mobile home registration also runs through the Supervisor. The title must be valid and taxes current, and moving a title at the Secretary of State takes a tax certificate from the Treasurer.

The deadline is 30 days after assessment changes for your township are published. Deliver the complaint and evidence to the assessment office before 4:30 p.m. that day, or mail them postmarked no later than it. Talking to the assessor does not pause the deadline.

Common stumbling blocks:

  • One complaint per parcel, on the Board's own form. Faxed and emailed complaints are refused.
  • Attach one copy of your evidence. Writing that no evidence is provided will probably bring a no-change decision.
  • You can contest the assessment but not the tax amount.
  • Missing items trigger a notice and 10 days to fix them.
  • Hearings are by appointment, last about 15 minutes, and take no new evidence.

The County Board appoints the Board of Review's three members, and the Board starts meeting by the first Monday of June. A written tentative decision comes to you, and a hearing request must be made inside the period shown on it.

Staff at the assessment office verify eligibility, and some exemptions need fresh proof yearly. What is available:

  • Owner-occupied homestead: $6,000 off assessed value when the owner lives in the house.
  • Senior citizen: a further $5,000 once the owner reaches 65, with proof of age.
  • Senior freeze: holds the value at the first qualifying year for owners already on the senior exemption, with household gross income of $65,000 or less in assessment year 2025 and $75,000 or less from 2026.
  • Homestead improvement: shelters the added value from a garage, porch or deck on an owner-occupied house for four years.
  • Returning service members: $5,000 off the main residence for two straight years.
  • Service-connected disability: $2,500 at a 30 to 49% rating, $5,000 at 50 to 69%, and full exemption at 70% or above.
  • Persons with disabilities: $2,000, renewed with annual proof.

The first two dollar amounts match the state statutes for counties not adjoining one of 3,000,000 or more (35 ILCS 200/15-175 and 15-170).

Search your parcel on the county tax lookup, match it to the bill in hand, and call the Treasurer about any open installment. At closing the title company prorates the year, and the settlement statement lists what is paid, owed or held in escrow. Your lender, if it escrows, can report what it has remitted.

Earlier years left unpaid complicate a sale. Find out from the County Clerk if the taxes were sold and what it costs to redeem, because whoever holds the certificate must be paid before title clears. Redemption generally lasts three years after the sale, subject to exceptions (35 ILCS 200/21-350). A cash buyer can close on the payoff numbers from those two offices, which keeps the schedule short when back taxes are involved.

faqs.q: Which number reaches the Logan County Treasurer?
faqs.a: 217-732-3761, for bill questions and past-due amounts. The office is in courthouse Room 11 in Lincoln.

faqs.q: How much is the late penalty in Logan County?
faqs.a: Real estate tax adds 1.5% per month after a missed due date. Mobile home tax adds $25 after June 1 and $25 each month more, up to $100.

faqs.q: Does the Logan County Treasurer accept cards?
faqs.a: For real estate tax, yes: at the counter, by phone at 217-203-8359 or online. The counter fee is 2.35% plus $1.50, and phone callers need the property index number.

faqs.q: What is the appeal window for a Logan County assessment?
faqs.a: Thirty days after your township's changes are published. File by 4:30 p.m. or postmark by that day, using a separate form for each parcel.

faqs.q: Where do I get the Logan County homestead exemption?
faqs.a: Contact the Supervisor of Assessments at 122 N. McLean St., Lincoln, 217-732-9635. The owner-occupied exemption is $6,000 off assessed value.
